第 22 章 Don't Just Evaluate Candidates on Skills别只靠技能评估候选人

Jay Signorello / 杰伊·西尼奥雷洛

— 第 69 页 —

The penalties for hiring the wrong people can be enormous. So, it's critical that you, as a manager, put a great deal of effort into creating and continuously refining your interview process with the goal of finding exceptional people. In the pursuit of finding great people, your focus areas for evaluating candidates will be one of the most important ways to differentiate between the best and worst candidates.

招错人的代价可能是巨大的。所以，作为经理，你投入大量精力创建和不断完善面试流程、目标是找到优秀的人，这至关重要。在寻找优秀人才的过程中，你评估候选人的重点领域将是区分最好和最差候选人的最重要方式之一。

It's not uncommon for a new manager to focus exclusively on skills required for the position. They craft their tests to determine whether the candidate has knowledge in a particular programming language, framework, and other technical areas. As they begin interviewing, they'll get a false sense of security when they find many people who can't complete the test, thinking that they're doing a good job of filtering out poor candidates. Then, one candidate will come along and breeze right through the test. The manager thinks to themselves, "Wow, this person must be amazing." So, they quickly hire them.

新经理只关注职位所需技能并不少见。他们设计测试来判断候选人是否具备特定编程语言、框架和其他技术领域的知识。开始面试时，当他们发现很多人做不完测试，会产生一种虚假的安全感，以为自己在很好地筛选差的候选人。然后，一个候选人出现了，轻松通过测试。经理心想：「哇，这人一定很厉害。」于是赶紧招了。

After a month or so on the job, however, the manager receives feedback from their team that this employee is difficult to work with and closed minded. Now the manager has their work cut out for them. They'll need to work with the employee on interpersonal skills and try to align them on the team's values. These rarely change for most people. So, not surprisingly, the employee becomes upset over their manager's feedback. And the problems only grow worse from there.

然而，工作一个月左右后，经理收到团队反馈说这个员工很难合作、思想封闭。现在经理有得忙了。他们需要和员工在人际交往技能上下功夫，试图让他们对齐团队价值观。这些对大多数人来说很少改变。所以，不出所料，员工对经理的反馈感到不满。问题只会从那里变得更糟。

Our job as managers is to avoid these sorts of problems altogether by putting together a team that works incredibly well together. Team members should play off one another's strengths and weaknesses while also sharing common values. To accomplish this, you'll need to instead focus your evaluations on values, abilities, and skills (in that order).

作为经理，我们的工作是通过组建一个合作得非常好的团队来完全避免这类问题。团队成员应该互补彼此的优缺点，同时共享共同价值观。要做到这一点，你需要把评估重点放在价值观、能力和技能上（按这个顺序）。

— 第 70 页 —

Values are a person's principles or standards of behavior. For example, a person might value the ability to move quickly or continuously learn new technologies. If your organization is at odds with a candidate's values, there will always be tension in the relationship. So, it's important that your organization defines and documents its own values. Your team should take those values and rank them based on what's most important to their group's particular needs. The more values that are aligned, the higher the likelihood the candidate will excel in the team and organization.

价值观是一个人的行为原则或标准。例如，一个人可能重视快速行动或持续学习新技术的能力。如果你的组织和候选人的价值观不一致，关系中总会有张力。所以，你的组织定义并记录自己的价值观很重要。你的团队应该根据团队特定需求对这些价值观排序。对齐的价值观越多，候选人在团队和组织中表现出色的可能性就越高。

Abilities are the things that come easy to people. Their inherent talents. For example, a person can be detail oriented or, conversely, able to look at the "big picture." Certainly, anyone can be detailed or see things from a higher level. But those who don't have those abilities need to work extra hard to have the same level of quality. Incorrectly evaluating these will result in your time being spent constantly monitoring the consistency of quality for an employee, which is unlikely the best use of your time.

能力是人天生擅长的东西。他们的内在天赋。例如，一个人可能注重细节，或者相反，能够看到「大局」。当然，任何人都可以注重细节或从更高层面看问题。但那些不具备这些能力的人需要额外努力才能达到同样的质量水平。错误评估这些会导致你把时间花在不断监控员工的质量一致性上，这不太可能是你时间的最佳利用方式。

Values and abilities aren't areas you can question a candidate about directly. Imagine asking a candidate whether they value moving quickly. What is the probability they will answer that they value moving slowly? Low. Candidates are unlikely to admit they lack an ability. Worse, some misaligned candidates will tell you that they agree with your values, but will do everything they can after being hired to change them. This will require you as a manager to create tests that evaluate on default behaviors while also assessing their track records. For example, when your organization values continuous learning, you should be asking how they've demonstrated it previously. You could also ask them to share resources they've recently used to gain a new skill. If the candidate has difficulty coming up with examples, it's a big red flag.

价值观和能力不是你可以直接问候选人的领域。想象一下问候选人是否重视快速行动。他们回答重视缓慢行动的概率是多少？很低。候选人不太可能承认自己缺乏某种能力。更糟的是，一些价值观不一致的候选人会告诉你他们同意你的价值观，但入职后会尽一切努力改变它们。这就要求你作为经理创建基于默认行为的测试，同时评估他们的过往记录。例如，当你的组织重视持续学习时，你应该问他们之前是怎么展示这一点的。你也可以让他们分享最近用来学习新技能的资源。如果候选人举不出例子，那是个很大的危险信号。

It's understandable why managers gravitate toward skills evaluations. They're straightforward to test on. Just remember, though, skills are also the easiest area for an employee to improve upon. Great employees will be excited to take on new learning challenges. All you'll need to do is allocate some time for them to gain those skills, either in projects or through dedicated time.

经理倾向于技能评估是可以理解的。技能测试起来很直接。但请记住，技能也是员工最容易提升的领域。优秀的员工会兴奋地接受新的学习挑战。你只需要分配一些时间让他们获得这些技能，无论是在项目中还是专门的时间里。

Evaluating on values and abilities is more difficult at the outset, but it pays large dividends in the end, making it worth the extra work.

从价值观和能力评估一开始更难，但最终会带来巨大回报，值得额外的努力。
